subject: Assessment kit lease and recall protocol
messages:
From: Sanjay Patel <sanjay@evallabs.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 31 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Assessment kit lease — ops + next steps

Hi Dylan + Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As discussed, Eval Labs is prepared to provide a scoped assessment kit (testcases + promptpack) on a short-term lease so your QA/evals team can run closed-loop runs against the Redwood runtime. We want to make sure usage is governed (no re-sharing, ephemeral-only, and a planned recall window).

Attached is the initial package: assessment-pack-v1.zip (contains 2K test cases, prompt templates) and a short README (promptpack-README.pdf). We also uploaded the MAP draft to the shared Drive link below.

High level asks from our side:
- Lend: 30-day ephemeral lease with an option to extend one time for 15 days.
- Usage: non-production only, internal evals; no dissemination outside Redwood eval team.
- Audit: weekly consumption snapshot emailed to ops@evallabs.com.
- Recall: fast-takedown clause if material misuse is detected (48 hours).

Can you confirm if that aligns with Redwood's take? If yes, Marissa suggested we put the MAP+operational ledger into a quick DocuSign and loop in legal.

Sanjay
Sanjay Patel
Head of Integrations, Eval Labs

Attachments: assessment-pack-v1.zip (archive, 18MB)
             promptpack-README.pdf (1p)
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Patel <sanjay@evallabs.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 31 May 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Assessment kit lease — ops + next steps

Thanks Sanjay — this looks good as a starting point. A few follow-ups from our side:

1) Technical access: we'll want the package in a read-only bucket and a short manifest (file hashes + provenance) so our infra team can validate integrity before ingestion.
2) Ephemeral policy: Redwood can host the kit in a restricted sandbox tied to a single eval project and a short-lived service account. We'll implement automatic token expiry to enforce the 30-day window.
3) Audit cadence: weekly snapshots are fine; can we pin the snapshot format (CSV: file, rows consumed, tokens generated) so monitoring is consistent?
4) Recall SLA: 48 hours is acceptable; please confirm escalation contact for legal if a recall is triggered.

Marissa — can you take point on drafting the MAP doc (legal + ops bullets) and share with Logan for the ingestion checklist?

I'll coordinate the infra side to prepare the sandbox.

—Dylan
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Patel <sanjay@evallabs.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 31 May 2026 11:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Assessment kit lease — ops + next steps

Sanjay — uploading a slightly edited MAP draft (MAP-draft-20260531.docx) to the Drive link; key changes in this version:
- Added the recall procedure (contact list, legal triage timeline).
- Defined acceptability gates: no production data, no model fine-tuning against the kit without express written permission.
- Added a short operational ledger section (who ingests, who runs experiments, snapshot retention).

Proposed MAP timeline:
- Day 0: Redwood confirms sandbox and service account. Ingest manifest + run integrity check.
- Day 1–7: Smoke tests and one acceptance run with our QA prompts.
- Day 8–30: Full evaluation window (30 days). Weekly snapshots sent to ops@evallabs.com.
- Day 30: Automatic lease expiry; artifacts remain encrypted and slated for deletion unless a single 15-day extension is approved in writing.

Please review the MAP draft in the Drive and flag any redlines. If that timeline looks good, I'll prepare a short DocuSign (MAP + ledger) to lock the operational terms.

Marissa
Senior Partnerships Manager, Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: MAP-draft-20260531.docx (Drive)
From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 31 May 2026 13:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Assessment kit lease — ops + next steps

Couple of technical constraints to call out for the MAP/ingestion checklist:

- Ingest manifest should include SHA256 for each file and a CSV mapping test-case-id -> prompt-template id. That makes it trivial to produce weekly consumption deltas.
- We will run the kit only on isolated GPU nodes (no external network egress during runs) to satisfy the ephemeral requirement.
- Token accounting: we can export tokens/generated per test-case but will need to cap retained inference logs to 90 days for storage reasons. If Eval Labs requires longer retention, we need a signed exception.
- If any promptpack uses external private keys or connectors, we must refuse ingestion.

I'll add these bullets to the MAP draft before Marissa sends to DocuSign.

—Logan
Lead Platform Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Sanjay Patel <sanjay@evallabs.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 01 Jun 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Assessment kit lease — ops + next steps

Appreciate the quick turnaround, team. The timeline and constraints look sane. A few confirmations from our side:
- We'll add SHA256 hashes and the test-case->prompt mapping to the manifest before upload.
- No private connectors in the pack.
- Ops contact for recall: legal-incident@evallabs.com (also looping in our head of security, Priya Rao).

Please go ahead with the DocuSign when Marissa is ready. We'll countersign and aim to have the kit available in the shared Drive by EOD Thurs (2026-06-03).

Thanks — looking forward to the runway.

Sanjay
Head of Integrations, Eval Labs
